parsed.why: Protective shield, public accommodation, open documents and care access raise in-state exposure; dated male-facility custody harm and hostile national border keep it elevated, not safe.
Strongest traveler-facing regime: shield law, public accommodation, identity-congruent custody and documents; national passport/custody exposure still caps score.
State birth-sex facility rules, marker narrowing, pronoun-disclosure and mixed city protections worsen mean regime slightly below national, but no criminal enforcement and existing legal recognition.

Hostile mean regime: bathroom restrictions, no public-accommodation/hate protection, care bans and document denial, with thin recourse, materially worsens national border risk though no trans-specific campaign.

Protective public accommodation, gender-neutral facilities, shield law and open markers materially lower in-state risk; no documented custody policy and national passport/entry exposure keep it elevated.
